verses.p: Pray for each family member by name and declare together: as for me and my house, we will serve the LORD.

verses.v: Therefore if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old things have passed away. Behold, all things have become new.
verses.p: Celebrate that they are a new creation, and invite them to read a passage with you each week.

verses.v: No temptation has taken you except what is common to man. God is faithful, who will not allow you to be tempted above what you are able, but will with the temptation also make the way of escape, that you may be able to endure it.
verses.p: Help them find the way of escape, and encourage them to have a spiritual companion for accountability.

verses.v: but those who wait for the LORD will renew their strength. They will mount up with wings like eagles. They will run, and not be weary. They will walk, and not faint.
verses.p: Affirm that their waiting is not wasted; ask God to renew their strength in it.

verses.v: Trust in the LORD with all your heart, and don’t lean on your own understanding. In all your ways acknowledge him, and he will make your paths straight.
verses.p: Help them place a decision in God’s hands and seek his will together.

verses.v: shepherd the flock of God which is among you, exercising the oversight, not under compulsion, but voluntarily; not for dishonest gain, but willingly; not as lording it over those entrusted to you, but making yourselves examples to the flock. When the chief Shepherd is revealed, you will receive the crown of glory that doesn’t fade away.
verses.p: Encourage a co-worker: you are not a hired hand but the Lord’s shepherd, and the Chief Shepherd will remember you.

lp.v: I am the good shepherd. I know my own, and I’m known by my own;
lp.p: Write what you know about this person: family, work, current situation, spiritual state, biggest need.
lp.e: Ming, 35, two kids, under heavy pressure at work lately, often late to meetings, irregular in Bible reading.

lp.v: The gatekeeper opens the gate for him, and the sheep listen to his voice. He calls his own sheep by name and leads them out.
lp.p: Pray for them by name, asking the Holy Spirit to show you their real needs.
lp.e: Lord, I bring Ming before you by name. Show me the burden on his heart.

lp.v: Whenever he brings out his own sheep, he goes before them; and the sheep follow him, for they know his voice.
lp.p: Where do you hope they will grow? How will you live it out first as an example?
lp.e: I hope he reads the Bible daily; I will keep my own daily reading and share what I learn each week.

lp.v: He said to him the third time, “Simon, son of Jonah, do you have affection for me?” Peter was grieved because he asked him the third time, “Do you have affection for me?” He said to him, “Lord, you know everything. You know that I have affection for you.” Jesus said to him, “Feed my sheep.
lp.p: Choose a passage or lesson that fits them and plan how to feed them (one-on-one, small group, sharing).
lp.e: Call him for twenty minutes every Tuesday evening and read a passage of Mark together.

lp.v: I will seek that which was lost, and will bring back that which was driven away, and will bind up that which was broken, and will strengthen that which was sick; but I will destroy the fat and the strong. I will feed them in justice.
lp.p: Are they weak, sick, hurt, driven away, or lost? What kind of care do they need?
lp.e: He is more “weak” right now; he needs steady encouragement, not rebuke.

lp.v: I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep.
lp.p: What concrete cost are you willing to pay for them? When will you follow up?
lp.e: This month I will give him one extra hour a week; in two weeks I’ll take him to dinner.

five.v: Rejoice with those who rejoice. Weep with those who weep.
five.p: Ask about their week; listen for joys and struggles. Focus on the person before the material.
five.e: How was your week? What are you thankful for, and what has worn you out?

five.v: Every Scripture is God-breathed and profitable for teaching, for reproof, for correction, and for instruction in righteousness,
five.p: Read a passage slowly, each reading once, and find the line that speaks to you.
five.e: Let’s read this together. Which line stands out to you most?

five.v: So, then, my beloved brothers, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, and slow to anger;
five.p: Ask open questions and let them speak first; then humbly share your own insight.
five.e: What does this passage show you about God? What is it saying to you?

five.v: But be doers of the word, and not only hearers, deluding your own selves.
five.p: Help them choose one concrete action they can do this week, and agree to share next time.
five.e: What is one practical way you want to live out this verse this week?

five.v: ‘The LORD bless you, and keep you. The LORD make his face to shine on you, and be gracious to you. The LORD lift up his face toward you, and give you peace.’
five.p: Pray for each other, send them off with a blessing, and set your next time.
five.e: The LORD bless you and keep you. See you same time next week.

min.v: Search me, God, and know my heart. Try me, and know my thoughts. See if there is any wicked way in me, and lead me in the everlasting way.
min.d: Pray first and ask the Spirit to search your heart and guide your words. Learn their situation, prepare a verse and a small gift, set a time, and bring a co-worker when appropriate.
min.s: (In your heart) Lord, I’m not going to fix this; love them through me.

min.v: So, then, my beloved brothers, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, and slow to anger;
min.d: Open with open-ended questions and listen to their story and feelings. Don’t interrupt or rush to advise; reflect back now and then.
min.s: “How have you been doing lately?” “I hear that you’re…, is that right?”

min.v: Rejoice with those who rejoice. Weep with those who weep.
min.d: Respond to their feelings so they know you understand. Quiet presence is fine; you don’t have to fill every silence.
min.s: “That sounds really hard. Thank you for telling me.”

min.v: Your word is a lamp to my feet, and a light for my path.
min.d: When they are ready, gently share a promise or read a short psalm together. Never preach at them with Scripture.
min.s: “There’s a verse that carried me through a hard season. May I share it?”

min.v: ‘The LORD bless you, and keep you. The LORD make his face to shine on you, and be gracious to you. The LORD lift up his face toward you, and give you peace.’
min.d: With permission, pray briefly, specifically and with faith; touch only the shoulder, and close with a blessing.
min.s: “May I pray for you?” “The LORD give you peace.”

min.v: Bear one another’s burdens, and so fulfill the law of Christ.
min.d: At home, note their needs and anything you promised. Keep confidences, check in within three days, and refer to a pastor or professional help when needed.
min.s: “I’ll keep praying for you and call you in a couple of days.”

rules: Be shepherded first
Return to the Good Shepherd every day, and have your own pastor and spiritual companions.
The sheep are the Lord’s
Say “the sheep the Lord entrusted to me,” not “my members”; people are not your achievements.
People over tasks
Never hurt people for the sake of programs, or break relationships over things.
Listen before speaking
Listen more, talk less; asking beats guessing. Don’t rush to answers or preach with verses.
Be an example, not a boss
Invite rather than command; never control through pressure, guilt or spiritual authority.
Keep confidences
What is shared in care stays private; get permission before sharing at prayer or team meetings.
Respect boundaries
Bring a companion when visiting the opposite sex; set times for visits; touch only the shoulder; avoid being alone late at night.
No condemnation, no guarantees
Never say “you lack faith” or “you will surely get well”; respect medical and professional care.
Work as a team
Don’t carry everything alone; always let your pastor know about serious situations.
Glory to God
When sheep grow, it is God’s grace; when they leave, keep praying. Give thanks in all things and give Jesus the glory.

s: Check in
Ask about their week; listen for joys and struggles.
Read together
Read a passage slowly; each finds the line that speaks to them.
Share insights
Let them speak first with open questions, then share yours.
Set an action
Help them choose one doable action for this week.
Pray and bless
Pray for each other, bless them, and set the next time.
Devotional sharing
Read a passage; each shares one line of insight.
Flock updates
Share updates on those you shepherd; flag who needs care.
Assign care
Decide who visits, who calls, and who needs referral to a pastor.
Support each other
Share how the team members are doing and pray for one another to prevent burnout.
Pray for the flock
Pray for the flock by name and give glory to God together.
Meal and welcome
Eat or have tea together; especially welcome newcomers and greet one another.
Icebreaker
Use a simple question so everyone speaks, such as “one thing you’re thankful for this week.”
Worship
Sing two or three songs and turn everyone’s focus to Jesus.
The Word
Read a passage or use this lesson; discuss See, Think and Do questions.
Pray for one another
In twos or threes, share requests and pray for each other.
Send and bless
Recall this week’s action and who needs care; pray the Lord’s Prayer or bless each other.

timer.p: Set everything down and return to the Good Shepherd; let him shepherd you first.
Let God be God: praise him as the Good Shepherd and Chief Shepherd.
Let people be people: confess where you treated the sheep as your own or overlooked someone.
Open My Flock and pray for each person by name.
Be still: whom is the Spirit leading you to care for this week?
Hand the flock to the Chief Shepherd and thank God for their lives.
